q1_issues.issue: The sealed complement of "judged that the dim burning was equivalent..." carries no tense atom at all, but sequence of tense keeps a past-tense verb's (Past ...) inside the seal, so the reified equivalent-state and its flat half should be past-marked.

"burned dim" is encoded as a class atom on the burn event itself, whereas the instruction set routes a bare adjectival secondary predicate as a depictive concurrent state on the subject ("arrived tired") or as a Manner atom, not as a Member atom on the event witness.

q2_gaps: A day-of-year date in a non-Gregorian calendar ("day 111 of Year 1"): the (Day <n>) term is specified as the day-of-month of a calendar date, and no convention is given for an ordinal day-of-year with no month, so (Day 111) is indistinguishable downstream from a day-of-month reading.

An adjective that is simultaneously a symmetric predicate and takes a PP complement ("was equivalent to an untended night"): the adjective's-PP-complement reification rule and the symmetric-predicate rule (which explicitly names "is equal to") both claim it, with no tie-break, and there is no guidance on whether a (Symmetric ...) tag may sit inside a seal.
notes: Coreference (the lantern, the wick, "the dim burning"), the "that night" term-propagation, the in-place-of Beneficiary, and the did-not-trim denial bundle are all handled per the instruction set. Whether the surface-fused agent-nominalization compound substitute_keeper should also carry (Inheritance substitute_keeper (can keep)) is arguable under the fixed-firing rule.
